reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) supports that ultrasonic burnishing (UB) produces gradient nanostructures and compressive residual stress in various alloys, but it does not provide specific evidence for TC4 (Ti6Al4V) or for the effect of a subsequent 400°C annealing step on retaining the nanostructure in this alloy. The Hall-Petch and residual stress mechanisms are textbook knowledge and need no citation, but the annealing premise lacks direct support.
premises: SMAT/UB can produce a gradient nanostructured surface layer with refined grains on alloys
SMAT/UB induces compressive residual stress in the near-surface
Grain refinement enhances hardness via the Hall-Petch effect
Compressive residual stress improves wear resistance
Low-temperature annealing (~400°C) relieves stresses while preserving nanostructure in TC4
